pages.title: Release runbook
pages.author: arjun.mehta
pages.content:
# Release runbook

Steps the release manager follows each month. Background: https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/releases/release-managers/

1. Two weeks before release: create the release branch and the checklist issue.
2. Tag a release candidate every weekday and deploy it to staging.
3. If the staging QA stage fails, check the runner pool first (see engineering#1).
4. Release day: tag the final version, deploy, and post release notes in #engineering.
5. Hand over open problems to the next release manager.

pages.title: Parental leave case handling
pages.author: carlos.mendes
pages.content:
# Parental leave case handling (HR process)

How People Ops handles a parental leave request. The policy itself is public: https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/leave-types/

1. The team member submits the request in Workday 30-45 days before the leave.
2. Absence Management confirms eligibility for the 16 weeks of paid parental leave and any statutory leave in their country.
3. The People Business Partner checks the manager has a coverage plan.
4. Payroll is notified of the leave dates and any statutory top-up.

pages.title: Enterprise EMEA playbook
pages.author: james.oconnor
pages.content:
# Enterprise EMEA playbook

- Qualify on three things: team size, self-managed vs SaaS, and compliance needs.
- For SSO or compliance questions, bring in a Solutions Architect (Ravi Kumar) early.
- Run a POC only with written success criteria (see sales#1 for a good example).
- Log every deal update in the sales project.
